# Theme Author Guide

This guide is for people who make or share their own themes. The first part walks you through your first theme with no coding experience needed. The rest is a reference: every colour, picture and part a theme can change, and the safety rules every theme follows. To pick, try, import or remove a theme, see [Custom CSS Themes](custom-css-themes.md).

**Token contract version 1** (`--mari-tokens-version: 1` on `:root`). The names in this guide keep working between releases. When one has to change, the version goes up and the change is listed under [Changes](#changes) at the end. Everything else (other `--ov-*`, `--mari-*` and `--marinara-*` variables, Tailwind classes, element structure) is internal and can change in any update.

## Your first theme, step by step

A theme is a short list of settings written in CSS, the language web pages use for colours and fonts. You don't need to know CSS to start. Each line looks like `--name: value;`: a **token** (a named setting that starts with `--`), a colon, the value, and a semicolon.

1. Open **Library → Settings → Appearance** and click **CSS Themes** in the row of sections.
2. To change a starter theme, download one you like from **Browse the theme gallery**, find it under **Starter themes** and click **Clone + Edit** (the copy icon). Marinara makes your own copy, named for example "Petal OS (my copy)", and opens it in the editor. Starter themes stay read-only, so the original is always there. To start from scratch instead, click **Create Theme**. Its template has lines between `/*` and `*/`, which are switched off. Delete those marks around a line to switch it on.
3. Type a name in the name box.
4. Change a colour. Find a line such as `--primary: #3fae7a;` and replace the colour. `#3fae7a` is a hex colour code. Any colour picker on the web gives you one. Names such as `teal` work too.
5. Leave **Preview** on. The app changes as you type, so you see each change at once.
6. Look under the editor. **No CSS problems found.** means the CSS is fine. Otherwise each problem shows with its line number, such as a missing `;` or `}`.
7. Click **Save**. Your new theme turns on, and Marinara asks **Keep this theme?** Click **Keep theme** within 15 seconds, or it goes back to your old look.

The tokens most people change first:

| Token            | What it colours                              |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `--background`   | The page behind everything                   |
| `--foreground`   | Main text                                    |
| `--primary`      | Buttons, links and highlights                |
| `--card`         | Cards and panels                             |
| `--sidebar`      | The chats and Library sidebars               |
| `--border`       | Lines around things                          |
| `--mari-font-ui` | The app font, for example `"Georgia", serif` |

A small theme:

```css
:root {
  --mari-tokens-version: 1;
  --primary: #3fae7a;
  --mari-selected-tint: var(--primary);
  --mari-font-ui: "Inter", system-ui, sans-serif;
}

[data-theme="dark"] {
  --background: #0f1712;
  --card: color-mix(in srgb, #0f1712 80%, transparent);
  --sidebar: #0b120e;
}
```

`:root { … }` holds settings for every colour scheme. `[data-theme="dark"] { … }` holds settings for Dark only, and `[data-theme="light"] { … }` for Light only. To see the full list of tokens while you work, open **CSS Variable Reference** under the editor, or read [Colour tokens](#colour-tokens) below.

### Add pictures and fonts

Open **Pictures and sharing details (author, version, thumbnail, fonts)** under the editor and click **Add pictures**. Click a picture's name to put it in your CSS at the cursor. See [Pictures](#pictures) and [Backdrops](#backdrops) for where pictures can go.

Pictures and fonts must be inside the theme. A theme can't load anything from another website, so a link to a picture or a Google Font in your CSS won't work.

### Ask Professor Mari to make the art

If you have an image model set up in **Connections** (Codex, NovelAI, ComfyUI, an OpenAI image model and so on), Professor Mari can make a theme's pictures for you and put them in it. Ask her in plain words, for example "make my Harbor theme a night-sky backdrop" or "give the Home cards a brass frame".

1. Mari works on your own themes only. For a starter theme, click **Clone + Edit** first and ask her to work on the copy.
2. She writes the picture prompt herself and sends it to your image model exactly as written. Your image style profiles and prompt prefixes (usually set up for character art) are left out, so a backdrop doesn't come back as a portrait.
3. You see each picture before anything changes. Ask for a few versions to pick from (up to 4 at a time), or for fixes such as "crop it to the top half", "make the white background see-through" or "make it smaller". Each fix is a new version, and the earlier ones stay.
4. When you say yes, Mari saves the picture into your theme (as WebP, the same way **Add pictures** does) and puts it in the theme's CSS. It shows up under **Pictures and sharing details** like any picture you added yourself.

Each picture takes as long as your image model needs, often half a minute to a minute and a half. If your image connection uses your own ComfyUI workflow, text built into that workflow is still sent.

### Share your theme

1. In **Pictures and sharing details**, fill in **Author**, **Version** (such as `1.0`), **Description** and **Thumbnail**, and pick **Made for** (Dark, Light or both). To suggest your colours and font along with the theme, click **Use my current Appearance** under **Settings**. Save.
2. Click **Export** (the upload icon) on your theme's row. Marinara saves one `.json` file with the CSS, pictures and fonts inside.
3. If you used art or fonts someone else made, open the file in a text editor and add credits and a licence. See [Theme files](#theme-files).
4. Send that file. The other person imports it with **Import File** and sees your name, credits and a list of anything the theme changes before they install it.

### If something goes wrong

Marinara keeps the top bar, the sidebars, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>K</kbd> and the message box usable whatever a theme does. If your theme hides, moves or covers one of them, Save tells you what broke. You can still choose **Save anyway**, but Marinara switches the theme off in a tab as soon as it breaks one. To get your normal look back at any time, press <kbd>Esc</kbd> three times, add `?safe` to the end of the address, or press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>K</kbd> and type "Custom theme".

Starter themes are good examples to learn from. Clone one and read its CSS to see how it uses the tokens and part hooks below.

## How a theme wins

The app's own CSS sits in cascade layers, declared first thing in `index.html`:

```
mari-protected, mari-theme-important, theme, base, components, utilities, mari-app, mari-pickers
```

- A theme is **unlayered**, so a plain selector in a theme beats every app rule without `!important`,
  whatever the app rule's specificity.
- `mari-pickers` holds the Appearance pickers (background, accent, fonts, chat colours). It sits
  above the app's defaults and below a theme, so a theme's colours win over the pickers, and
  Appearance tells the user when a theme overrides a picker.
- `!important` in a theme still works. Those rules are copied into `mari-theme-important`, which
  beats the app's own `!important` rules.
- `mari-protected` keeps the top bar, the chats sidebar, the Library sidebar and Ctrl+K in place.
  A theme can restyle them (colours, fonts, borders, radius, shadows) but not hide, move, shrink or
  cover them. If it tries, the theme is switched off in that tab and the user is told why.

The way back always works: `?safe` in the URL, **Escape three times**, or Ctrl+K > "Custom theme"
turns the theme off. A new theme asks "Keep this theme?" and goes back after 15 seconds.

## Colour tokens

### Core (every visual style defines these)

`--background`, `--foreground`, `--card`, `--card-foreground`, `--popover`, `--popover-foreground`,
`--primary`, `--primary-foreground`, `--secondary`, `--secondary-foreground`, `--muted`,
`--muted-foreground`, `--accent`, `--accent-foreground`, `--destructive`, `--destructive-foreground`,
`--border`, `--input`, `--ring`, `--radius`, `--sidebar`, `--sidebar-foreground`, `--sidebar-border`,
`--sidebar-accent`, `--sidebar-accent-foreground`.

Values are full CSS colours (`#1b1530`, `rgb(…)`, `oklch(…)`). Bare HSL triplets such as
`270 25% 8%` (the shadcn convention) are **not** valid here.

Scope light and dark separately with `[data-theme="light"]` and `[data-theme="dark"]`.

### New layout

| Token                                                            | Used for                                                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--ov-line`                                                      | Hairlines and panel borders                                                                                                   |
| `--ov-text`, `--ov-muted`, `--ov-dim`                            | Text, secondary text, faint text                                                                                              |
| `--ov-accent`                                                    | Accent spots (defaults to `--primary`)                                                                                        |
| `--ov-hover`, `--ov-active-bg`                                   | Hover and pressed backgrounds                                                                                                 |
| `--ov-mode-conversation`, `--ov-mode-roleplay`, `--ov-mode-game` | Chat-mode colours in the chats sidebar and editors                                                                            |
| `--ov-serif`                                                     | Title font (follows `--mari-font-heading`)                                                                                    |
| `--mari-selected-tint`                                           | Selected rows, pills and toggles. Neutral (`--foreground`) by default; set it to `var(--primary)` for accent-tinted selection |
| `--mari-selected-bg`, `--mari-selected-ring`                     | Derived from the tint (10% and 18%)                                                                                           |

### Theme tokens (v1)

Each one defaults to the app's own look. Light mode has its own readable values.

| Token                                                                                                    | Used for                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--mari-font-ui`                                                                                         | The whole app's font                                                                                                        |
| `--mari-font-heading`                                                                                    | Page and section titles                                                                                                     |
| `--mari-font-chat`                                                                                       | Message text in roleplay and conversation chats                                                                             |
| `--mari-mode-conversation`, `--mari-mode-roleplay`, `--mari-mode-game`                                   | Home chips, recent chats, the new-chat launcher, Home widget eyebrows                                                       |
| `--mari-home-pink`, `--mari-home-violet`                                                                 | The other Home widget accents                                                                                               |
| `--mari-status-online`, `--mari-status-idle`, `--mari-status-dnd`, `--mari-status-offline`               | Presence dots and labels                                                                                                    |
| `--mari-gauge-ok`, `--mari-gauge-warn`, `--mari-gauge-danger`                                            | Game gauges and HP bars. A widget's own colour still wins in its normal state; danger always uses the token                 |
| `--mari-game-combat`, `--mari-game-combat-text`                                                          | The game's Combat button                                                                                                    |
| `--mari-stage-empty-bg`                                                                                  | The game stage before a scene image loads (any `background`, gradients included)                                            |
| `--mari-scrim`                                                                                           | The dimmed backdrop behind Ctrl+K                                                                                           |
| `--mari-user-avatar-placeholder`                                                                         | Your avatar when you have no picture (a gradient)                                                                           |
| `--mari-art-saturation-1`, `--mari-art-lightness-1`, `--mari-art-saturation-2`, `--mari-art-lightness-2` | The gradient on cards without a picture. Each card keeps its own hue; set these (as percentages) to calm the gradients down |
| `--mari-app-backdrop`                                                                                    | An image or gradient behind the whole app, painted once (see below)                                                         |
| `--mari-accent-fx-animation`                                                                             | The Accent Pulse or RGB Mode animation while one is on, otherwise `none`                                                    |

### Theme tokens added in v1.1

These have no value until a theme sets one, so the user's own setting applies until then.

| Token                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Used for                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--mari-text-outline`                                                                                                                                                                                                        | The outline on message text, for example `0` to turn it off or `1px #3b2a1a`. Otherwise it's the user's Text Outline setting

Set `--mari-app-backdrop` on `:root` to paint art behind the app:

```css
:root {
  --mari-app-backdrop: url("theme:city.webp");
  --mari-app-backdrop-position: bottom center;
  --mari-app-backdrop-rendering: pixelated;
}
```

It is drawn once, on its own fixed layer under the whole app (`[data-mari-part="app-backdrop"]`, so
Home's decorations and the light scheme never hide it), and it shows behind chats too: the roleplay,
conversation and game surfaces go transparent and the stock chat background steps aside. A
background the user picked for a chat still shows on top of it. Panels keep `--card` and
`--sidebar`, so make those translucent if you want the art to show behind them, and use
`--mari-page-veil` to tint full pages. To give pages a panel of their own, style
`[data-mari-part="page"]` (see Hooks): it holds every Library page, editor, Settings and Docs, so
Lorebooks gets the same panel as Characters.

| Token                            | Default                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
